issues.legal_issue: A family’s land-ceiling holding is determined by its membership on the applicable notified date, and land belonging to a daughter who was no longer part of the family on that date cannot be clubbed with the widow’s holding.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned whether the widow’s and daughter’s land together exceeded the applicable ceiling for a family holding.
The daughter had married before the notified date under the amended law and was no longer a member of the widow’s family on that date.
The authorities nevertheless clubbed the daughter’s land with the widow’s land when determining surplus land.
issues.conclusion: The daughter’s land could not be clubbed with the widow’s land because the daughter was no longer part of the family on the notified date.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 17 of 1970, the family holding had to be determined by reference to the state of affairs on the notified date. Since the daughter had married before that date, the family then consisted solely of the widow. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: The authorities were determining whether land held by a family exceeded the applicable land ceiling.
predicates.daughter_not_family_member_on_notified_d: The daughter had married before the date used to assess the family holding and was no longer a member of the widow’s family on that date.
predicates.daughter_land_excluded_from_family_holdi: The daughter’s land was not included in the widow’s family holding.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling proceeding concerns a daughter who was no longer a family member on the assessment date, her land is excluded from the family holding.

issues.legal_issue: A saving provision for action taken in earlier land-ceiling proceedings does not support a later proceeding that conflicts with the favorable outcome of those earlier proceedings on the same subject matter.
material_facts: An earlier land-ceiling proceeding resulted in the Tribunal setting aside the officer’s order and holding that the widow’s land could not be clubbed with the daughter’s land.
The officer later issued a fresh notice concerning the same land and whether it should be included in the family holding.
The later proceeding resulted in a determination that the family held surplus land.
issues.conclusion: The saving provision did not assist the respondents; the later notice and proceedings were quashed, and no further proceedings could be taken on the same subject matter.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 17 of 1970 provides that qualifying action taken under the principal Act may be enforced as if the amending Act had not been passed. The Court held that this provision supported the holder because the outcome of the original proceedings before the Tribunal had been in her favor. No earlier cases were relied on.
